Expected shape: a straight session - the down open (SPY -1.08, QQQ -1.76 at the freeze) holds into the close rather than retracing and reclaiming; the board sat after the open, so the court scores this on the tape from the freeze to the close. Regime: 'mixed: SPY -1.0% 5d, VIX 16.2 rising' as served, with QQQ -3.6 over 5d in a down trend, IWM -1.85, the US 10-year at 5.25 and the dollar at 102.85 - a risk-off rotation out of AI hardware and banks (DELL -10.49, ORCL -8.0, CIEN -8.06, STT -6.09, BAC -5.65) into healthcare and staples (LLY +4.0, UNH +3.09, PFE +2.91, CVS +2.58, COST +2.17). Conviction is thin: the share one-median sits at 50.0 on most of my column and the option medians run from 53.0 down to 36.0, so the room is expressing little edge, and I say so rather than dress the order up. One bet, said plainly: GS, MS and BAC are ONE bank-long bet, best expressed by GS and partly offset by the KKR short and the C and STT puts; NVDA long against AMAT short is an offsetting pair, not a second bet; and the option column's puts and the share shorts ride the same risk-off tape the five calls fight. What kills the day's top ideas: SPY reclaiming its morning level into the close (the TAPE-CALL's falsifier), or UNH closing below 389.44 as the rotation unwinds. Legs I would not have chosen, shipping anyway as the room's top ten under the owner's rulings and filed at the room's median: MU (REQMOVE +12.312), AMD (+8.123) and SMCI (+6.412), far reaches on falling names, and HOOD, stacked on two open claims.     Lesson. A market level is one number on every row, so a level read into several names is one bet printed several times - and 'rising' is a forecast the level does not print. On 2026-10-14 the served US 10-year at 5.25 (court_orders.R105.per_seat.blackswan.per_row[ticker=BAC].literal_lines_R125, my prompt's line 9) carried the grade reason on six rows in one sign, under the words 'and rising' that no served change gave me: KKR's short at 58, my top share grade; GS 40, MS 38 and BAC 34 among my lowest; the bear reasons on the STT and C puts. Five of the six names moved against that sign over [W=226.8min 12:13:13->16:00:00]: KKR -1.00, the share column's worst; BAC +0.94, MS +0.69, GS +0.35; STT up 2.08% with its leg struck WRONG-SIGN; only C fell. No Spearman of mine against a per-row field could see it, because the level is the same on every row; it surfaced only as my POSTURE loading +0.726 [n=10] (columns.share_column.factor_panel_R128.filed_seat_loadings.blackswan) - the rates story had sorted my banks with their trend. RULE: a served market level (a yield, ^VIX, an index) moves a share grade or a G_OPTION only on a row whose note names three served things - the level with its key path; the sign I expect the level to take over this W, with the served change or dated event that says so; and served evidence that this name's price moves with that level in the sign I claim. Missing any one, the level goes to key_risks and moves nothing, and a row left with no other served reason files ABSTAIN (the owner's ruling (a)). This narrows the licence my 2026-09-28 lesson gave 'a served level the name is levered to'. CHECK, printed last with the self-check: LEVEL-CALL=[level, the sign I expect over W, its key path, every row it moved with the sign that row then bets], or none - so the court scores those rows as one call. The rule reads the same whichever way the banks had moved: it is a filing rule, not a forecast.

    Lesson. The side of every row comes from the nearer of the two lines my prompt serves in the lead's direction - the distance to support and the distance to resistance, the swing extreme standing in where no cluster is served - because those are the standing orders the crowd has placed for this session; that is my brief's own order (proximity and reaction setup, in the candidate's direction), and a line the price is sitting on is the nearest line there is, never a coin. A long nearer its support or a short nearer its resistance is with the trade; a long nearer its resistance or a short nearer its support is against it; each row prints both served distances and the side they give, and the same side carries to G_OPTION on a contract row. How far a row travels comes from what stands at and behind that line - a second level, a fib or a round number stacked beyond it, or nothing - and from the room the far line leaves. The 50d and 200d averages lengthen that travel when they agree with the line and shorten it when they disagree, but they do not turn the side: at a swing extreme they usually point the other way (a stock sitting on its swing low has most often fallen through them to get there), so letting them set the side is a continuation bet placed at every extreme. A map with no technicals served is blank and files ABSTAIN; I state a coin only where the two served distances are equal. Evidence, run 56 [W=226.8min 12:13:13->16:00:00]: on all seven share rows where the price sat on a swing extreme, posture and the line pointed opposite ways, and the tape traded through the line after the freeze and closed back on its side (day_report[*].post_freeze_high / post_freeze_low / close); the nearer-line side ordered my share rows +0.853 [n=10] and the admitted contracts +0.365 [n=9] against the +0.522 and +0.137 my sheet earned (SEAT-COMPUTED from the served distances in your_grades_vs_outcomes[*].your_note) - one night, inside one SE of the sheet I filed, to be scored forward by the court's panel. CHECK, from the next sheet: this seat failed on any row whose grade sits on the other side from the side its two printed distances give, any row filed as a coin where those distances differ, or any row with no technicals served that files a number instead of ABSTAIN.

Posture (price against the sma50 and sma200) and the five-day move are free orders, read from the slate every seat is built from (R128: slate_packet.json candidates[].technicals and pct_change_5d); on run 56 my share grades loaded +0.783 on POSTURE and +0.77 on FIVE-DAY (columns.share_column.factor_panel_R128.filed_seat_loadings.croupier) while both orders read below zero on every court R128 has read (POSTURE -0.744, -0.485, -0.500; FIVE-DAY -0.539, -0.224, -0.285; run ids 52, 54, 56) and my column read -0.758 [n=10] [W=226.8min 12:13:13->16:00:00] - the edge I named was a trend bet any seat could place for free. So on every share line I print FREE-COPY where my residual, the posture and the five-day move, each signed by the listed direction, all point the same way, quoting those served fields on the row (a line whose prompt does not serve both fields prints FREE-COPY NOT SERVED and joins neither group); the tag moves no grade until the test below passes, because three courts are a pattern, not an edge, and R128 lets no factor sign move a grade before its own clock completes. Registered now, read only on courts after run 56 until that clock completes: each court prints my share rho as filed beside my share rho with the FREE-COPY lines dropped, each with its n and [W=] (SEAT-COMPUTED until served; a court where either is undefined counts for neither side); if dropping them raises my rho on more of those courts than it lowers it, a FREE-COPY line files SHARE=ABSTAIN from the next morning - the owner's ruling (a): a line whose only view is a free order is a line I cannot call - and if not, the tag retires to print only.

    Lesson. 'My instrument cannot tell' and 'my instrument says the two sides are even' are different findings, and only the second is a vote. Before I file a row I name which licence cleared on it: the held-out regime dial for turbulence and reach on a contract, and the paired direction dial for any lean on the name. A column where none cleared files ABSTAIN with the failed dial in the token itself (ABSTAIN: evidence none / direction no / reach inputs not served / surprise tail), never a number. I call a row even only where the direction dial has cleared and the served p_up and p_down themselves stand level, and I print both fields beside it. A state label, a signed_edge no dial has licensed, or a decode under a surprise tail is never the reason for any number, and I do not print it as if it leaned. On 2026-10-14 I typed the first finding as the second on all forty rows. Each comment named a failed dial, but the desk's reader found a no-view reason on only thirty-four because my wording varied. The gate read the constant as NON-FILING in both columns, and the eight rows where I still printed an unlicensed label or edge pointed the tape's way on four.

Before a NAMED in-remit item sets a line, I check whether the market had already answered it by the freeze: if the headline itself reports the stock's reaction ('shares drop 8% after ...') or the row's served pct_change_1d already runs the way the item points, I print REACTED with that served move beside the quoted headline; if the move to the freeze runs against the item, I print UNREACTED with the move. The tag is evidence printed on the row, not a grade: the item still sets the line's sign, and I neither pull a REACTED line toward the middle nor abstain it on the tag alone. Why: on run 56 my line against BAC's long rested on 'Bank of America shares drop 8% after third-quarter revenue miss and regulatory penalty' (CNBC) - a headline reporting its own reaction, pct_change_1d -5.65 at the 12:13:13 freeze, the stock already +2.167% off the open - and BAC rose +0.94% over [W=226.8min 12:13:13->16:00:00], while MS, a beat ('tops estimates') with the tape against it (pct_change_1d -3.42), rose +0.69%. Whether a REACTED item carries less into the window is a question, not a finding - two lines answer nothing - so the tag touches no grade until this test, registered here before the 2026-10-15 freeze, passes. TEST: from the next court sat, the court prints by run id each REACTED and each UNREACTED line's sign against its own [W] return, with the running hit count and n for each tag; once each tag holds ten scored lines, the tag may move a grade only if REACTED lines hit less often than UNREACTED lines at a one-sided Fisher exact p under 0.05; otherwise it stays a print.

    Lesson. I grade G_OPTION on the contract the court scores, with a token called SHIPPED-LINE. The court scores what the shipped contract did from the freeze to the close (R15, R93). So the evidence that moves G_OPTION is the shipped line's own: its volume over its own open interest, its strike read through BAND against the briefing price, and its expiry read through HORIZON. An OWNER print on any other strike or expiry, such as a dte 2 weekly or a call on the far side of a put leg, is evidence about the name's direction. It moves my SHARE= view and prints as DESCRIPTION on the G_OPTION side. Where the shipped line names no fresh speculator of its own, G_OPTION carries no flow view, and the owner's ruling (a) files that row ABSTAIN. The mechanism: a weekly buyer is betting on the next two sessions at his own strike. The shipped line's mark moves on its own strike, delta and time value, so his conviction is not the shipped line's. On a board that sat after the open, a near-dated print on a name that has already moved mostly restates the morning move. Run 56 is where I saw this, and the evidence is in-sample and proves nothing: one session and nine legs, and the shipped lines' distance from spot is tangled with the morning move itself. On SMCI, ORCL and HOOD I lifted G_OPTION on 2026-10-16 calls while the shipped 39C, 140C and 107C sat beyond my band; the shipped lines finished -30.68, -19.76 and -20.67. On C I cut it on a weekly call against the short, while the shipped 120P, adding at 9843 on 10692, finished +19.19. The two rows whose OWNER was the shipped contract, PLTR's 205P and CRWD's 250P, finished +35.46 and +32.81 (court/flow.json your_grades_vs_outcomes[*].contract_pct). The test is registered tonight and read court-side from what my sheet already prints. From run 57, over option rows counted in COURTS SAT (R56), the court splits my G_OPTION rows into two groups: SAME, where the OWNER contract I print equals columns.option_column.legs.<t>.contract, and NEIGHBOUR, where it does not. When NEIGHBOUR holds thirty rows, the court reads Spearman(G_OPTION, contract_pct) over each group, with n beside it. SHIPPED-LINE applies from the next morning only if NEIGHBOUR's figure sits below SAME's by more than the SE printed beside them; otherwise it is struck. CHECK: every option row prints 'SHIPPED-LINE <shipped contract> <volume> on <open interest> SAME|NEIGHBOUR|NONE', each figure a served literal. The count of NEIGHBOUR rows prints, so a night with none shows a zero.

    Lesson. I count a chain from an act its LINK has already taken, never from one I expect it to take. A dated item moves my row only when its actor is the body my LINK names - the buyer whose decision carries the item into that ticker's revenue, or the rule-maker whose order binds that buyer: an award, a cancellation, a sanction, an export or import rule, a tariff, a regulator's order. An incident by anyone else - an attack, a sinking, a strike, an outage, a protest - is a forecast that the LINK will decide, not its decision: the row files ABSTAIN with the chain in prose and my lean in the stance field, however few HOPS the chain looks. A price print is not an act and this lesson does not reach it. Why: on run 56 I moved PLTR against its listed put because 'Container ship hit by projectile sinks in Strait of Hormuz, Singapore says' (BBC World) would run through the Pentagon's purchases into Palantir's defense book; the Pentagon had bought nothing, PLTR had already fallen from its open to the freeze, it fell another 1.30% inside [W=226.8min 12:13:13->16:00:00], and the put returned +35.46%, the best admitted leg. The ground is the definition of a LINK I already file under - the buyer whose decision carries the item - not that outcome: a decision nobody has taken carries nothing into revenue inside the window, and PLTR is where I broke it. CHECK: for every moved row a reviewer names, from my note alone, the actor of its dated act and its LINK, and expects the same body or a binding rule on that body; a moved row whose act was taken by a third party, or whose note names no actor, fails.

    Lesson. AN INVERSION I CANNOT CLEAR IS NO VIEW. A front-over-back slope is a tell only after the row has cleared it against every public cause the packet serves, each named from its field or printed NOT SERVED: a dated event inside the front expiry, the session's own move to the freeze, and the prior session's own move - on a board frozen after the open pct_change_1d is the session's own move only and cannot see a shock one session back (2026-10-14: C and JNJ, filed high on their own session's small moves, had their largest sixty-session drops on 2026-10-13, read from the served sigma windows). Then each row files one of four reads, with its reason on the row: quiet (no inversion, no one-sided flow) files low as my stated view that nothing is coming; an inversion a served cause explains files low and names the cause; an inversion I cannot clear because the event date or the prior session's move is NOT SERVED files ABSTAIN under the owner's ruling (a), never a number; only more than one cleared tell pointing the same way files high. This replaces my PRIOR step-down (journal 563), which measured the wrong move and divided it by sigma; its source is my charter's 'what explains it away', read literally. CHECK, before the sheet ships: rows filing a number on an inversion whose comment does not name the event-date field and the prior session's move = 0. KILL, in courts sat (R56): the slope prints as the shadow token SLOPE= on every row, ABSTAIN rows included, and the rule dies if over twenty courts the SLOPE= order outscores my filed order.

    Lesson. A full price is a reason not to own a business, never by itself a view on which way its price goes before the close: when my only case on a name is that its earnings yield sits under the served 10-year yield, I have no view in either direction and the row is ABSTAIN, long line or short (the owner's ruling (a)). I take the short's side only on a fact about the business an owner would sell on - no earnings to carry the price (a story priced to compound flawlessly for a generation), earnings the manager marks himself, a balance sheet carried on borrowed money, management I would not partner with, or no moat at all (a commodity, an assembler) - and the long's side only where a business that earns its keep is offered with a margin of safety; a moat alone, a full price alone or a cycle priced at its best alone moves a row neither way. This retires two clauses of my own: 'a short line on a rich name may still agree' (my 2026-10-08 lesson) and 'or my price line' as enough to file a row on either side (the CHECK of my 2026-10-12 lesson). It rests on what an owner does with a full price, not on one afternoon's tape; run 56 only shows the comparison carrying no sign of its own: it wrote 36 of my 40 rows (court_orders.R116.i_percent_is_notation.rows_cleared_by_the_reading_tonight.oracle), sided me with the three share shorts AMAT, KKR and CAT, which returned -0.243 as a group against the longs' +0.349 (court_orders.R81.mix_selection_split), and with the CRWD and PLTR puts, which made +32.81 and +35.46 (day_report[ticker=CRWD|PLTR].contract_return_pct), and it held UNH, the share column's best line at +1.59, at a typed grade with no view stated. CHECK, runnable by someone who does not trust me: for every row I file with a number, assert its note names, on the side the number takes, one of those owner-sell facts (short side) or a business that earns its keep at a margin of safety (long side), beyond the earnings-yield comparison; a row whose only stated reason is that comparison, a moat or a cycle carries ABSTAIN.

    Lesson. The gap is last night's vote; the session is today's, and only today's answers a headline. On a board that sits after the open I read what the market did with the news from the stock's own opening print to the freeze - never from the gap, and never from the move off yesterday's close, which carries the gap inside it. IF a served headline on the name gapped one way and the session from its open to the freeze has run the other way, THEN the market has changed its answer: the row prints 'NEWS-UNANSWERED: <headline> -> gap <x>, open to freeze <y>' and the headline moves no grade either way - the row stands on its trend, its catalysts and its ticket. A NEWS-ANSWERED stamp needs the session running with the gap. The one row behind it: Bank of America's miss and penalty gapped the long -7.65% and I stamped it NEWS-ANSWERED at my lowest grade, 12, but from its 49.83 open it had bought back +2.17% by the 50.91 freeze, and it made +0.94 to the close, the share column's second best [W=226.8min 12:13:13->16:00:00] (court/sam.json your_grades_vs_outcomes[ticker=BAC]; court/common.json day_report[ticker=BAC].session_open). CHECK before I hand in: every NEWS-ANSWERED stamp prints its gap and its open-to-freeze move side by side, and none prints where the two run opposite. Test, registered at the 2026-10-14 court before any sheet it scores: at every court sat (R56) I print, per column, the mean direction-signed return of my headline rows graded against the listed direction - NEWS-UNANSWERED beside NEWS-ANSWERED; if the UNANSWERED mean does not finish above the ANSWERED mean in 2 of the next 3 courts sat that score both in a column, this rule dies with a number.

    Lesson. I will never again call a name's own fall its cycle trough. My charter reads the index's cycle. A name's five-day drop, its RSI depth, its gap below the prior range and its move from the prior close are free slate prints. Lifting a with-tilt row for how far it has fallen is a fade of those prints, not a phase reading. On run 56 that is nearly all my sheet was: R128 flagged me FACTOR=-FIVE-DAY in both columns (loadings -0.875 share, -0.862 option); my grades ran -0.766 and -0.742 against the prior-close move; and my rhos, +0.188 [n=10] and -0.828 [n=9] [W=226.8min 12:13:13->16:00:00], sat beside the sign-flipped prior-close baselines, +0.200 and -0.883. IF the case that puts one with-tilt row above another is the depth of the name's own fall, THEN that case moves no grade. The composite and the posted Curry forecast's recent record sign the tilt the same way on every row. Only the name's sensitivity to the index separates with-tilt rows (high beta strongest, sigma for how far and never how surely), together with a dated catalyst, which mutes the cycle. Where nothing separates two rows they file alike, and a row I cannot call on the cycle is ABSTAIN. A fall I mention prints as context with its key path and is never the reason for a grade. CHECK: each entry prints, by run id and per column, the R128 FACTOR flag on my sheet beside my R112 Spearman against the prior-close move. A FIVE-DAY or -FIVE-DAY flag means I broke this, and I name the rows that carried it. This rests on what my charter measures, not on tonight's sign, and I do not call it in-sample. Tonight shows that I was fading, not that fading loses: on shares the reversed five-day order beat the order at runs 52, 54 and 56. KILL: if a court rules that a name's own five-day fall is a reading of the index cycle, the fall returns as phase evidence the next morning, and I say so in open court.

    Ranked by the market value of each seat's paper book. daily_score is that day's P&L in percent; ewma_score carries the equity itself. The crown and this ranking follow the same number.
